name: Bipolaris leaf spot
summary: A confirmed hemp leaf-spot and blight disease caused by Bipolaris gigantea. Necrosis can become severe, but lesion appearance overlaps Septoria, Cercospora, Alternaria, anthracnose, and abiotic damage.
affectedParts: buds secondarily when blight is severe
indicators: Necrotic leaf spots expand and can contribute to broader leaf blight
Disease can become widespread in outdoor hemp
Compatible lesions occur with Bipolaris conidia or molecular evidence from affected tissue
exclusions: Cercospora-type conidiophores and white-centered round spots dominate
A chemical or physical injury pattern follows an exposure boundary
Laboratory testing identifies a different leaf-spot pathogen

progression.description: Lesion number and necrotic area increase across foliage.
Severe cases can involve broad tissue necrosis and canopy loss.

confirmation: Use fungal morphology and molecular identification from representative lesions for organism-level confirmation.
Record field distribution and lesion progression; one photograph is insufficient for B. gigantea.
immediateActions: Preserve symptomatic tissue for diagnosis before discarding representative samples.
Separate diseased material from clean propagation stock.
correctivePlan: Apply confirmed leaf-spot disease management appropriate to local rules and production conditions.
prevention: Reduce infected crop residue and prolonged leaf wetness where feasible.
Scout field plantings for early leaf spots.
warnings: Bipolaris leaf spot can look like several other Cannabis leaf-spot diseases.
Yield impact varies by cultivar, season, and disease complex.

sources.title: First Report of Hemp Leaf Spot Caused by a Bipolaris Species on Hemp (Cannabis sativa) in Kentucky
supportedClaims: Outdoor hemp in Kentucky developed severe necrotic leaf spot and blight associated with a Bipolaris lineage corresponding to Drechslera gigantea/Bipolaris gigantea.
Inoculated hemp leaves developed symptoms while noninoculated controls remained symptomless, and molecular loci supported placement in Bipolaris.
The report supports Bipolaris leaf spot as a Cannabis-specific disease but requires pathogen evidence for species-level confirmation.

sources.title: Leaf Spot Disease Development and Its Effect on Yield of Essential Oil-Producing Hemp Cultivars in Kentucky
supportedClaims: Bipolaris, Cercospora, and Septoria were the prevalent hemp leaf-spot diseases evaluated in Kentucky field trials.
Septoria generally appeared first, followed by Bipolaris, while Cercospora developed later in reproductive stages; cultivar susceptibility varied.
Overlapping leaf-spot syndromes mean distribution, timing, microscopy, culture, and molecular diagnostics are more reliable than one lesion photograph.
